header: One Gemini reading of one page, with everything the service says about it (step 39d). The app does not use it. I wrote it to find out WHY a page's read is slow or never comes back (seen on 19 Oct 2026: page 1 of a circular read in 13 s while page 2 of the same upload hung through three attempts of 50 s). It sends exactly the request the upload sends (same instructions, temperature 0), waits as long as it is told, and reports the time, how the answer ended, how many tokens went to the page, to the answer and to "thinking", and whether the answer repeats itself. I made the two knobs that could change the behaviour (the answer's length limit and the thinking budget) options, so a hypothesis costs one command and touches nothing in the app. Pure apart from the injected fetch. Unit-tested by geminiProbe.selftest.ts. Used by scripts/gemini-probe.ts.

members.name: timeoutMs
doc: I wait this long for the answer, in ms (default 300 000).

members.name: maxTokens
doc: The answer's length limit in tokens (default 8192, the same as the upload sends).

members.name: thinkingBudget
doc: Tokens the model may spend thinking (0 = none). I leave it out of the request when undefined, so the service's own default applies.

members.name: looped
doc: True when the answer repeats itself (the reader would cut it at the loop).

symbols.sig: export function compareProbes(a: ProbeResult, b: ProbeResult): string
doc: I put two reads of the SAME page side by side (A: as stored, B: shrunk): the time, the size sent, and whether the important numbers agree.

behaviours: a normal answer: ok, HTTP 200, finish reason STOP, text kept
the tokens are reported: page, answer, thinking, total
no repetition is reported for a normal text
the request is the upload's: the same instructions, temperature 0, the page as inline data, the key in a header
by default the answer limit is 8192 and no thinking setting is sent (the service's own default)
the address is the model's generateContent address
--max-tokens sets the answer limit
--thinking-budget 0 is sent (0 is a real value, not 'unset')
another address is used when given
a request that never answers is abandoned at the timeout and says so
an HTTP error is reported with its status and what the service said
a network failure is reported
an answer that repeats one line is flagged
an answer cut at the length limit reports its finish reason, and missing token counts say so
a 429 body of more than 800 characters is kept whole (the quota id is at the end of it)
the report adds one plain line on which limit it was
another HTTP error gets no quota line
the report names the page, the request, the time, the tokens and the ends of the text
a failure is reported on one line with the time
comparison: the times, the sizes sent, the speed-up and that the numbers agree
comparison: a number that differs is named on both sides
comparison: slower is said plainly
comparison: a failed side makes it impossible, and says which
the script: exits 0 and prints the report
the script: the options reach the request and the report
the script: --jpeg-edge sends ONE read, a JPEG whose long side is at most 800 px and far smaller than the file
the script: --compare reads the page twice, as stored and then shrunk, and prints the comparison
the script: a service that never answers is abandoned at --timeout and reported as failed
the script: without a key it says what to do
